reasoning.title: Query State Isolation in Composed Queries and Combinators
reasoning.description: WHEN: Fixing bugs in union/intersection/difference operations, exclude() with annotations, or query chaining that produces unexpected results or state leakage between calls.
reasoning.content: Composed queries (.union(), .intersection(), .difference()) and split_exclude() create new Query objects that must be properly isolated from originals. Clone Query objects in _combinator_query() (django/db/models/query.py ~line 929) or get_combinator_sql() (django/db/models/sql/compiler.py ~line 428) before storing in combined_queries or modifying during compilation. When split_exclude() creates a new Query, copy annotations and _filtered_relations from the original: query.annotations = self.annotations.copy() and query._filtered_relations = self._filtered_relations.copy() (line 1668 in django/db/models/sql/query.py). Verify cloning via id() tracking across method calls to isolate whether bugs stem from shallow copying vs. state mutation during SQL generation.

reasoning.title: Minimal Reproduction Test Strategy for Django Debugging
reasoning.description: When investigating complex bugs, create a minimal reproducible test case FIRST before deep code exploration. This provides immediate feedback, prevents token waste on unfocused investigation, and establishes a clear validation target.
reasoning.content: Create a minimal test case early using existing test infrastructure (e.g., tests/annotations/tests.py, tests/model_inheritance/tests.py, or tests/migrations/test_autodetector.py) that reproduces the exact failure. Use Django's isolate_apps() or existing test models to avoid setup boilerplate. Run only the affected test class (e.g., `python tests/runtests.py auth_tests.test_checks.UserModelChecksTests.test_new_method`) rather than full suites. Once the bug is confirmed and root cause identified, implement the minimal fix immediately, then validate with existing tests—avoid exhaustive pre-submission verification when token budget is constrained.

reasoning.title: Use targeted grep searches to locate code quickly; avoid exhaustive exploration
reasoning.description: When investigating specific issues, use grep patterns to find exact code locations rather than reading entire files. Once the problematic code is identified, implement the fix immediately with a minimal test—avoid comprehensive exploration unless the fix requires understanding complex infrastructure.
reasoning.content: Use `grep -n 'pattern'` to locate specific methods, templates, or field-type checks in target files (e.g., `grep -n "template.*=" django/db/models/aggregates.py` for SQL templates, `grep -n 'def method_name'` for function definitions). Once you identify the exact line and understand the fix, implement immediately and test with a minimal reproduction case. Avoid reading entire large files (1000+ lines) or investigating secondary functions unless the issue explicitly requires it.

reasoning.title: Locate and fix issues using explicit file paths and minimal changes
reasoning.description: When an issue cites specific files, line numbers, or known patterns, go directly to those locations rather than exploring broadly. This prevents token waste and accelerates fixes.
reasoning.content: For Django settings issues (FILE_UPLOAD_*, etc.), edit django/conf/global_settings.py directly. For bugs with explicit file paths (e.g., django/db/backends/ddl_references.py#L87), start there and make surgical edits. For admin display issues, check django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_field() first. For migrations serialization, target django/db/migrations/serializer.py and tests/migrations/test_writer.py. Use grep/sed for exact line numbers, create a test case, apply the minimal fix, then run tests—avoid exploratory file reading and git history unless the fix requires understanding broader logic.

reasoning.title: Run existing test suite after implementation changes to catch mock/implementation mismatches
reasoning.description: WHEN modifying implementation code that has corresponding tests (especially mocking-based tests), BEFORE considering work complete. WHEN changing which function is called (e.g., subprocess.call → subprocess.run), verify mock targets match.
reasoning.content: Always execute the full test suite with the final patch: `python tests/runtests.py <app>` or `python -m pytest <test_file> -xvs`. Before finalizing, verify mock patch paths match actual function calls in implementation by grepping for the function name (e.g., `grep -r 'subprocess.run' src/`) and confirming mock decorators use the same target. This catches mock/implementation mismatches that break tests.

reasoning.title: Deletion optimization: minimize field fetching and ensure consistency across fast/normal paths
reasoning.description: When modifying django/db/models/deletion.py Collector class or adding deletion tests
reasoning.content: Use `.only('pk')` or `.values_list('pk', flat=True)` in related_objects() to fetch only primary keys and foreign key attnames (e.g., 'parent_id') needed for cascade logic, avoiding deserialization failures on problematic field types. The fast-delete path (single object, no cascades) must mirror normal-delete cleanup: explicitly set `instance.pk = None` after fast-delete query execution to match behavior at lines ~325–326. Add regression tests in tests/delete/tests.py verifying cascade deletion works with large text fields, binary fields, and encoding-sensitive data.

reasoning.title: Implement hook methods in Django framework classes: locate, pattern-match, then edit
reasoning.description: When adding customization hooks (like get_inlines, get_fields) to ModelAdmin or similar framework classes
reasoning.content: 1) Locate the target file and existing similar hook methods (e.g., get_fields, get_exclude) via single grep, then view 2–3 together to extract the pattern. 2) Place the new hook method immediately before the consumer method that uses it (e.g., get_inlines before get_inline_instances), returning the class attribute by default (e.g., return self.inlines). 3) Replace direct attribute access in the consumer with a hook call, passing the same request/obj parameters (e.g., change self.inlines to self.get_inlines(request, obj)). 4) Write a minimal test, then implement in one focused edit to avoid iterative cycles.

reasoning.title: Comprehensive Django Fix Verification Checklist
reasoning.description: Essential verification steps before submitting any Django patch, covering test execution, code inspection, regression detection, and completeness validation.
reasoning.content: Always complete the full test-verify-confirm cycle: run reproduction tests to completion with full output, execute the relevant test suite (`python /testbed/tests/runtests.py <test_label>` or `pytest tests/<module>/ -q`), and confirm zero failures before submission. Inspect generated patches with `git diff` for duplication, syntax errors, and missing logic branches. Search for ALL call sites of modified methods using `grep -r "method_name" /testbed --include="*.py"` and update them together. For security/default changes, verify corresponding checks in `django/core/checks/` are updated. Run final test suite one last time in the exact submission state—if tests fail, the fix is incomplete. Avoid iterative edge-case testing after core functionality is verified; submit once the reported issue passes and existing tests still pass.

reasoning.title: Database Backend Operations: Timezone, Duration, and Window Function Handling
reasoning.description: Consolidated patterns for fixing timezone-aware operations, duration field conversions, and window function casting across Django database backends.
reasoning.content:
**Timezone handling**: Examine `django/db/backends/{backend}/operations.py` for hardcoded timezone references in methods like `datetime_cast_date_sql()` and `_convert_field_to_tz()`. Verify `tzname` comes from `connection.timezone_name` (via `TimezoneMixin.get_tzname()` in `django/db/models/functions/datetime.py`), not global settings. For PostgreSQL's AT TIME ZONE, use regex `^[+-]\d[\d:]*$` to detect simple offsets and flip signs only for those; pass named timezones unchanged.

**Duration field conversions**: SQLite and MySQL return string representations from arithmetic expressions (e.g., '2 days, 0:00:00'). Override `get_db_converters()` in `django/db/backends/{sqlite3,mysql}/operations.py` to append a converter using `django.utils.dateparse.parse_duration()` before the base converter processes the value. Test with `Experiment.objects.annotate(duration=F('estimated_time') + timedelta(...))` patterns in `tests/expressions/tests.py` across all backends.

**Window functions on SQLite**: Check `window_compatible=True` in `SQLiteNumericMixin.as_sqlite()` before applying CAST wrapping. Window functions (Lag, Lead, FirstValue, LastValue, NthValue) require the OVER clause to immediately follow the function name, so skip CAST when this attribute is set.

reasoning.title: Navigate permission and search logic in django/contrib/admin/options.py

reasoning.content: Use `grep -n 'def has_.*_permission'` in `django/contrib/admin/options.py` to map permission methods across BaseModelAdmin and InlineModelAdmin (around lines 1960–2150). InlineModelAdmin overrides has_add/change/delete_permission to handle auto-created models by extracting the related model's _meta via foreign key fields and checking against that model's codenames. For search issues, examine `get_search_results()` around line 994, which constructs ORM lookups from `search_fields`, processes terms via `smart_split()`, and applies filters.

reasoning.title: Auto-created M2M through models need permission checks against the related model, not view permission

reasoning.content: For auto-created intermediate models in InlineModelAdmin, the has_add_permission, has_change_permission, and has_delete_permission methods should check the corresponding permission codename against the related model (not the through model), not delegate to has_view_permission. This prevents users with only view permission from being able to edit M2M inlines.

reasoning.title: Audit all code paths in methods with conditional returns for consistency

reasoning.title: Understand exponential notation cutoff logic in numberformat

When decimal_pos is provided, this cutoff may be overly conservative since the output is bounded by decimal_pos anyway. Check git history (commits e6d57c4d65, bc1c034076) for prior attempts to fix similar issues—they contain logic for comparing against a cutoff value based on decimal_pos that may be relevant.

reasoning.title: GenericForeignKey prefetch with non-integer PKs requires type coercion and test coverage

reasoning.title: PostgreSQL dbshell: Map SSL OPTIONS to environment variables, not CLI arguments
reasoning.description: When adding SSL certificate support to PostgreSQL's psql command in dbshell.
reasoning.content: Extract all four SSL parameters (sslmode, sslcert, sslkey, sslrootcert) from conn_params['OPTIONS'] and map them to psql environment variables (PGSSLMODE, PGSSLCERT, PGSSLKEY, PGSSLROOTCERT) in subprocess_env via a mapping dictionary—psql reads SSL config from environment variables, not command-line arguments. Follow the existing PGPASSFILE pattern and apply str() conversion for all assignments. This differs from MySQL (which uses --ssl-* flags) and is required for mutual TLS in strict security configurations.

reasoning.title: Test exclude() with annotated FilteredRelation before implementing fixes

reasoning.title: Preserve decorator and cache behavior when refactoring functions

reasoning.title: Constraint and Field Validation: Uniqueness, Lookups, and Manager Selection

For ForeignKey.validate() in django/db/models/fields/related.py (~line 918), use _base_manager instead of _default_manager to respect unfiltered querysets and allow forms to override with filtered objects. Test CheckConstraint SQL generation with mixed OR/AND operators in /testbed/tests/constraints/tests.py using _get_check_sql() to verify unqualified column references before migrations. Add regression tests to tests/validation/tests.py for ForeignKey validation with custom filtered managers.

reasoning.title: Django Testing: Use Existing Infrastructure and Test Both Code Paths

reasoning.title: Punycode conversion for non-ASCII domain names in email headers

reasoning.title: Bracket balance checking and loop completion in pattern parsing
reasoning.description: When iterating through characters to match brackets and process groups, ensure balance checks occur after counter updates and handle natural loop completion.

Adjust slice endpoint from `end + idx` to `end + idx + 1` to include the closing bracket. Use Python's for-else construct to append remaining pattern if the loop completes naturally without breaking and brackets are balanced, capturing groups that extend to the end of the string.

reasoning.title: Mutually exclusive groups and keyword-only arguments in Django management commands and template tags
reasoning.description: Fixes for argument parsing in call_command() and parse_bits() that fail to recognize arguments in required mutually exclusive groups and keyword-only parameters.
reasoning.content: In `django/core/management/__init__.py`, call_command() checks `opt.required` on individual actions but mutually exclusive groups store `required` on the group object (via `parser._mutually_exclusive_groups`); iterate through groups and ensure at least one argument from each required group is in `parse_args` if any group argument appears in `options` kwargs. In `django/template/library.py`, parse_bits() validates kwargs against `params` and `unhandled_kwargs` but must also check `kwonly` parameter; change validation from `param not in params and param not in unhandled_kwargs` to `param not in params and param not in kwonly`. Test both fixes in `tests/user_commands/tests.py` with required mutually exclusive groups and in template tag tests with keyword-only arguments (both required and with defaults).

reasoning.title: Widget attrs mutation and state isolation in form rendering
reasoning.description: When widgets modify their input attrs dict (especially CheckboxInput setting 'checked'), and that dict is reused across loop iterations in parent widgets like SplitArrayWidget, subsequent widgets inherit unintended modifications.

CheckboxInput.get_context() in django/forms/widgets.py directly modifies the passed attrs dict—this is unique among Django widgets. Test at form field level with actual Form/ModelForm classes and SplitArrayWidget rendering mixed True/False values to catch state leakage that unit tests miss.

reasoning.title: Enum serialization and value extraction in Django migrations and fields
reasoning.description: Handling enum members (Enum, IntEnum, TextChoices, IntegerChoices) correctly during migration serialization, field type conversion, and template rendering.

In TypeSerializer, use `__qualname__` instead of `__name__` to handle nested classes, rejecting those with '<locals>'. Add `cls.do_not_call_in_templates = True` in the enum metaclass __new__ method to prevent template invocation.

reasoning.title: Check git history first for regression fixes and prior attempts

reasoning.content: Use `git log --all --oneline | grep <keyword>` (e.g., issue number, 'regression', 'override', 'restore') and `git show <commit>` to find prior fixes. If a fix exists but isn't in HEAD, the testbed may be intentionally pre-fix. If already in HEAD, verify with existing tests rather than creating new ones. For specific problem areas, examine prior commits to understand what was attempted and the correct approach (e.g., field traversal logic, algorithm parameter handling) before implementing.

reasoning.title: Efficient root cause isolation for field behavior and reference issues

For ForeignKey/ManyToManyField 'app not installed' errors with mixed-case app names, check django/db/models/fields/related.py deconstruct() methods—use _meta.label_lower for app labels, lowercase only the model portion. reasoning.description: WHEN processing list/tuple values in Query.resolve_lookup_value() with sub-expressions, or pickling Query objects with values()/values_list(). WHEN NOT: non-iterable values or regular querysets without values().

reasoning.title: Keyword-only argument validation in parse_bits uses wrong variable
reasoning.description: WHEN checking if a keyword argument is valid in the `parse_bits` function in `/testbed/django/template/library.py` (around line 264), specifically when validating keyword-only arguments with defaults.

reasoning.title: Delegation patterns: verify method forwarding and GROUP BY preservation
reasoning.description: When wrapper classes delegate to wrapped objects, ensure both that delegation works end-to-end in real usage (not just unit tests) and that expression semantics are preserved.
reasoning.content: ExpressionWrapper must override get_group_by_cols() to delegate to self.expression.get_group_by_cols(alias), else wrapped constants incorrectly appear in GROUP BY. reasoning.title: Handle multiple exception types in DecimalField.to_python() and test with unexpected data types
reasoning.description: WHEN: A DecimalField.to_python() method receives invalid input types (dicts, lists, etc.) or invalid strings. WHEN NOT: Field only handles single exception type or tests only happy-path conversions.
reasoning.content: The Decimal() constructor raises TypeError (dicts/lists), ValueError (other unsupported types), and decimal.InvalidOperation (invalid strings)—not just one exception type. Wrap the Decimal() call in try-except catching all three (TypeError, ValueError, decimal.InvalidOperation) and convert uniformly to ValidationError using the field's 'invalid' error message. Include test cases for container types (dicts, lists, sets) in addition to invalid strings, as they expose gaps in single-exception handlers. For window functions with DecimalField, verify generated SQL has correct OVER clause syntax by running expressions_window tests on SQLite backend.

reasoning.title: ForeignKey attname vs field name in query resolution and SQL identifier quoting
reasoning.description: Covers ForeignKey field name resolution, SQL identifier quoting across backends, and type correctness in schema operations.
reasoning.content: In `names_to_path()` (django/db/models/sql/query.py), distinguish ForeignKey field access by attname (e.g., 'root_id') from field name (e.g., 'root') to prevent unnecessary JOINs and respect explicit order_by(). Always quote SQL identifiers using `self.ops.quote_name()` in backend-specific code (e.g., django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py) and PRAGMA statements to handle SQL keywords. In schema.py's `_create_unique_sql()`, pass `model._meta.db_table` (string) to `_index_columns()`, not a Table object, since Columns expects a string for proper references_column() behavior. For database routing, use the established pattern `router.allow_migrate(connection.alias, app_label)` from django/db/migrations/executor.py and django/db/utils.py.

reasoning.title: Validate database cursor results before subscripting in concurrent cache operations
reasoning.description: WHEN: Working with OFFSET-based cache culling queries or any database cursor operations that may return empty result sets due to concurrent modifications or conditional queries.
reasoning.content: Always check if `cursor.fetchone()` returns `None` before subscripting (e.g., `result[0]`). Use guard clauses like `if result is not None:` or `result and result[0]`. In cache culling with OFFSET queries, concurrent deletions can reduce table size below the offset, causing empty results between SELECT and DELETE statements—validate the culling query returned a row before using it in subsequent operations, or wrap in a transaction to prevent concurrent modifications.

reasoning.title: Cache backend culling is vulnerable to race conditions
reasoning.description: WHEN: Implementing or modifying cache backend eviction logic, particularly in `django/core/cache/backends/db.py` and similar multi-step database operations.
reasoning.content: Cache culling operations that count rows, then use that count in a subsequent query are inherently racy in concurrent environments. Between the count query and the offset-based fetch, other processes may delete rows, causing the offset to exceed available rows. Add defensive null checks and consider atomic operations or alternative culling strategies.

reasoning.title: Preserve cookie security attributes in delete_cookie()
reasoning.description: WHEN: Implementing cookie deletion that must maintain browser compatibility with SameSite/Secure/HttpOnly attributes and cookie name prefix conventions. WHEN NOT: Simple cookie operations without deletion or attribute preservation.
reasoning.content: Expand `delete_cookie()` in `django/http/response.py` to accept `secure`, `httponly`, and `samesite` parameters and forward them to `set_cookie(max_age=0)`. Use conditional logic to preserve automatic secure flag detection for __Secure- and __Host- prefixed cookies (e.g., `if not secure: secure = key.startswith(...)`) to prevent browser warnings about mismatched SameSite attributes and maintain backward compatibility.

reasoning.title: Optimize multi-pass post-processing to yield files exactly once with final hashes
reasoning.description: When implementing multi-pass post-processing (e.g., HashedFilesMixin.post_process()) where some files may change across passes while others are finalized early.
reasoning.content: In the first pass, yield only non-adjustable files immediately since they won't change in subsequent passes. Defer yielding adjustable files until the final pass where their hashes have stabilized. This ensures each file is yielded exactly once with its final hash value, eliminating the need to track duplicates across passes.

reasoning.title: Handle encoding and dependency migrations with backward compatibility
reasoning.description: When introducing session/serialization format changes or updating deprecated library parameters, ensure dual-path support and version compatibility.
